clue.text: London hospital about to admit posh horror writer

indicators.note: to admit means the reversed hospital takes something inside it
about tells us the hospital's name is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: Barts is the familiar name of St Bartholomew's Hospital in London
U means upper-class or posh, a well-known British usage

explanation.surface: A London hospital takes in an upmarket writer of horror stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BARTS into STRAB, and 'to admit' puts U inside it. Barts is St Bartholomew's, a London hospital; U for upper-class is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Straub is an American novelist known for his horror fiction, such as Ghost Story.

clue.text: Recurring theme in translated work by European

parts.note: op. (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: A recurring theme turns up in a European's translated work.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary motif or figure that keeps coming back is called by this critical term.

clue.text: Santos Vega was one in green at parties

indicators.note: parties is read as a verb, splitting up and parting the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A folk hero dressed in green at social gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' looks like a noun about celebrations but works as the verb 'parts', breaking up IN GREEN AT. Santos Vega is the legendary gaucho singer of the pampas, celebrated in poems by Mitre and Obligado.
explanation.definitionFit: Santos Vega, the legendary gaucho minstrel, was a national of the South American republic of Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Young man who was angry British shower broke ultimately

parts.note: a shower is a short fall of rain

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word broke

explanation.surface: An angry young man watches a British downpour break at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the 'Angry Young Men', the British writers of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: John Braine, author of Room at the Top, was grouped with the 1950s novelists dubbed the Angry Young Men.

clue.text: Play against good cricket side close to home

parts.note: anti means against
on, or leg, is one side of the field in cricket

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word home

explanation.surface: A play about a good cricket team playing near their home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is divided into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles wrote this tragedy about Oedipus's daughter who buries her brother against the king's edict.

clue.text: Work you might be able to find in the Karakoram Pass?

definitions.text: Work you might be able to find in the Karakoram Pass?

parts.words: Work you might be able to find in the Karakoram Pass?
parts.note: the Karakoram Pass is a route through the mountains leading into Ladakh on the Indian side, so a literary work's title is pictured as a mountain route

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a book could be found on a high Himalayan route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Karakoram Pass links Ladakh with Xinjiang: literally a way through to the subcontinent, and also the title of E. M. Forster's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster's 1924 novel about Aziz, Fielding and the Marabar Caves is a celebrated literary work.

clue.text: "Today's the day, gonna grab my — and blow" (Bob Dylan)

definitions.text: "Today's the day, gonna grab my — and blow" (Bob Dylan)

parts.words: "Today's the day, gonna grab my — and blow" (Bob Dylan)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation: the missing word is an instrument the singer grabs and blows

explanation.surface: A Bob Dylan line with a missing instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Dylan's 'Bob Dylan's 115th Dream'; 'blow' points to a brass instrument with a slide.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap needs a brass instrument played by blowing and moving a slide, which fits the eight letters.

clue.text: Travel diary brought over for chap famous for a diary

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: brought over means turned back to front, so the word for a diary runs backwards

parts.note: a log is a diary or journal kept on a voyage

explanation.surface: A travel journal is brought back for a famous diarist.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepys might spring to mind, but the diary here is fictional: Gogol's short story Diary of a Madman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian writer Nikolai Gogol wrote the story Diary of a Madman.

clue.text: "Rise the blue Franconian mountains, -, the ancient, stands" (Longfellow)

definitions.text: "Rise the blue Franconian mountains, -, the ancient, stands" (Longfellow)

parts.words: "Rise the blue Franconian mountains, -, the ancient, stands" (Longfellow)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from a Longfellow poem: the missing word is an old city in Franconia

explanation.surface: A Longfellow line about an ancient city with its name missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Longfellow's 'Nuremberg', which opens 'In the valley of the Pegnitz, where across broad meadow-lands / Rise the blue Franconian mountains'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Bavarian city in Franconia is the subject of Longfellow's poem of the same name.

clue.text: Aged major off to welcome old Brazilian author

indicators.note: to welcome means the rearranged letters take another inside them
off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly army major leaves to greet a veteran Brazilian writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles AGED MAJOR, and 'to welcome' puts O inside the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Jorge Amado wrote Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon and other novels of Bahia, making him a celebrated Brazilian novelist.

clue.text: Bloody abrupt English name Lincoln writer took on

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: gory means bloody

explanation.surface: A gory, short English name taken by a writer on Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrupt' cuts the Y from GORY. The writer of the novel Lincoln, Gore Vidal, was born Eugene Louis Vidal and took his grandfather's surname as a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal, author of the novel Lincoln, adopted his grandfather Senator Thomas Gore's surname as his first name.

clue.text: He wrote about a priest and some sober nanoscientists

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer about a priest is grouped with some temperate nanoscientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Bernanos wrote The Diary of a Country Priest, about a young curé in rural France.

clue.text: I'm able to change order in George Duroy's account

indicators.note: to change order tells us the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be capable of reordering a man's account.
explanation.walkthrough: George Duroy is the scheming hero of Maupassant's novel, whose story it tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Maupassant's novel tells the story of Georges Duroy, the handsome social climber.

clue.text: Old lady hot to turn around Albert Mission pupil

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, an old lady in slang

indicators.note: to turn around means the word for hot is read backwards

parts.note: in means hot, fashionable

explanation.surface: An elderly woman feels hot and turns to a famous missionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert' looks like a name for 'turn around', but Albert Mission School is the school in R. K. Narayan's Swami and Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: In Narayan's Swami and Friends, this boy is Swami's tough classmate at Albert Mission School in Malgudi.

clue.text: One who wrote dialogue and ace triolets for broadcast

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer of dialogue and expert verse forms going on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, with 'for' a link. Besides his treatises the philosopher wrote dialogues in Plato's manner, now lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher wrote dialogues in Plato's manner, praised by Cicero though only fragments survive.

clue.text: Comedian hanging around knight and Harry Starks?

indicators.note: hanging around means the comedian's name sits outside another letter

parts.note: a gagster is a comedian who tells gags
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A comedian loiters near a knight and a man named Harry Starks.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Starks is the East End gangster of Jake Arnott's novel The Long Firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Starks, in Jake Arnott's The Long Firm, is a 1960s London crime boss, an example of the type.

clue.text: Linesman finally removed after punching lowlife linesman

indicators.note: punching means one piece is driven into the middle of another

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible lowlife

indicators.note: finally removed means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet, is a writer of lines

explanation.surface: A line judge is sent off after hitting a lowlife linesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally removed' takes the S off BURNS, giving BURN, and 'punching' drives that into SWINE. Both 'linesman' words mean poet, not football official.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian poet, and a writer of verse lines is cryptically a linesman.

clue.text: You might say Armitage Shanks' third "Ultra-EE" potty

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
third points to the third letter of the word Shanks'

explanation.surface: A toilet maker's chamber pot is rated top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' rearranges A (third of SHANKS) with ULTRAEE. Armitage Shanks is a British maker of toilets; Simon Armitage is the Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Armitage became the UK's Poet Laureate in 2019, an example of the honour.

clue.text: American Agatha Christie rather upset outside home

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters sit around another piece
upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: An American crime writer is rather upset to be away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives the anagram REHART, and 'outside' puts it round the word for home. Rinehart's mysteries sold hugely in the 1910s-30s.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Roberts Rinehart, inventor of 'the butler did it' school of mystery, was often called the US counterpart of the Queen of Crime.

clue.text: I turn on Emilia in the end

definitions.text: I turn on Emilia in the end

indicators.note: on means placed after, following the previous letters
in the end means the final letter of the name Emilia

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they finally turned against Emilia.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes Othello's ensign, who kills his wife Emilia in the final scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the villain stabs his wife Emilia when she exposes his plot near the play's end.

clue.text: A red and black cap of English-designed pen from Nigeria

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, is a red
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: cap of means the top, first letter of the word English-designed

explanation.surface: A red and black pen cap designed in England comes from Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like part of the stationery, but it means a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinua Achebe, author of Things Fall Apart, was Nigeria's most famous novelist, and a pen is a writer.

clue.text: Early horror writer who helped to produce Inferno?

explanation.surface: An early horror writer who helped to create an inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferno' with its capital suggests Dante, but the second definition is a fireman who tends a boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula; and a furnace man feeding a fire helps make a blaze, an inferno.

clue.text: Kentucky party in which one might be given some stick?

definitions.text: in which one might be given some stick?

parts.note: Ken. is an old abbreviation for Kentucky
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party in Kentucky where someone might get a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given some stick' means criticised, but here literally hit with a bamboo sword.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese martial art is fenced with bamboo swords, so fighters are struck with sticks.

clue.text: Creep awful to pinch rear of cool simple story writer

parts.note: to inch is to creep slowly forward

indicators.note: to pinch means to grip, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: bad means awful

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of the word cool

explanation.surface: A dreadful creep steals from the back of a simple story writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch' suggests theft, but it means BAD gripping L.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Inchbald wrote the 1791 novel A Simple Story.

clue.text: Weapon chap with a salty wife's stolen from knight

indicators.note: stolen from means these letters are taken out of the knight's name

parts.note: Lancelot is a knight of the Round Table
Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man with a salty wife has a weapon stolen from a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by mounted knights is a classic weapon.

clue.text: Register taken back in Bertie Wooster's school

indicators.note: taken back means the word for register runs in reverse

parts.note: to note is to register or take notice

explanation.surface: A school register is returned at Bertie Wooster's old school.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's amiable idler, an Old Etonian.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster was educated at the English public school by Windsor.

clue.text: Writer with soldiers seen by edge of a new state?

parts.note: and means with, together
RE is the Royal Engineers, the soldiers
on the brink of a new state means on its edge or threshold

explanation.surface: A writer with soldiers stands on the edge of a new state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'new state' hints at the writer's South Africa after apartheid.
explanation.definitionFit: André Brink was an Afrikaans novelist, author of A Dry White Season.

clue.text: Info museum found about completed, but short, opera

indicators.note: found about means the museum is located next to the shortened word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: over means finished or completed
the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: Information from a museum about a complete but brief opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts OVER to OVE. The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum, written VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Schumann's only opera, from 1850, tells of the wronged medieval countess.

clue.text: I'm told Antigonus is one uncle of Henry the Fifth!

indicators.note: I'm told signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Antigonus in The Winter's Tale makes the most famous departure, 'Exit, pursued by a bear', so he is one who exits

explanation.surface: Someone hears that Antigonus is related to King Henry the Fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigonus is in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale; his stage direction 'Exit, pursued by a bear' makes him a famous one who exits.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Beaufort, Duke of Exeter, was Henry V's uncle and appears in Shakespeare's play.
